MICHAEL ENDE
幻想文学大师米切尔·恩德经典作品绘本
出走的绒布熊
撰文—米切尔·恩德
翻译—何珊
绘画—贝伦哈特·奥伯迪克
page_text_en:
MICHAEL ENDE
Classic Picture Book by Fantasy Literature Master Michael Ende
The Runaway Rag Doll Bear
Written by—Michael Ende
Translated by—He Shan
Illustrated by—Berndt Oberdieck
summary_zh: 本页为绘本《出走的绒布熊》的封面，展示了书名、作者米切尔·恩德、译者何珊、绘者贝伦哈特·奥伯迪克的信息，以及一只绒布熊和一只小老鼠的插图。
本页展示了一幅由多个绒布熊头像组成的重复图案，背景为深蓝色，每个熊头周围有细线和小飞虫，整体呈现出一种机械、单调的氛围，暗示主角绒布熊所处的工厂或批量生产环境。

page_text_ocr_zh:
从前，有一只可爱的旧绒布熊，他的名字叫小顽童。当他还是崭新的时候，耳朵上挂着一块小牌子，上面写着“小顽童”这三个字。于是，绒布熊的小主人就这么叫他。不过，这是很久以前的事了。现在，这个孩子已经长大上学去了，不再和绒布熊一块儿玩了。当然，时光的流逝，在小顽童的身上也留下了许多痕迹。他身上有的地方打上了补丁，由于经常梳洗，绒毛也已经磨坏了。
现在，大部分时间他都坐在沙发角上，那是专门给他安排的地方。他常常坐在那里发呆。可是，白天黑夜都在一个地方呆着不动，的确没有意思。所以，有时他也会悄悄地跳一会儿舞。不过，只有旁边没人时，他才会跳，否则他会觉得不好意思的，因为他确实不太灵活——和其他绒布熊一样。
page_text_en:
Once upon a time, there was a lovely old teddy bear named Little Rascal. When he was brand new, he had a little tag on his ear that said "Little Rascal." So, his little owner called him that. But that was a long time ago. Now, the child has grown up and gone to school, and no longer plays with the teddy bear. Of course, the passage of time has left many marks on Little Rascal. Some parts of him have been patched, and his fur has worn thin from frequent washing.
Now, most of the time he sits in the corner of the sofa, a spot specially arranged for him. He often sits there, staring blankly. But staying in one place day and night is truly boring. So sometimes, he quietly dances for a while. However, he only does this when no one is around, because he feels embarrassed, since he's not very nimble—just like other teddy bears.
summary_zh: 本页介绍了主角绒布熊‘小顽童’的背景：他曾是孩子心爱的玩具，如今孩子长大，他被遗忘在沙发角落，身上有补丁和磨损，偶尔在无人时悄悄跳舞，表现出孤独与渴望被关注的心情。

page_text_ocr_zh:
有一天，小顽童像往常一样坐在沙发角上。
这时，一只苍蝇在房间里“嗡嗡”地飞来飞去，
最后落在了他的鼻子上。
“你好！”苍蝇向绒布熊打了个招呼。
“你好！”小顽童回答说，并斜眼瞟了一下
鼻子上的苍蝇。
“过得怎么样啊？”苍蝇问。
“我坐在这里。”绒布熊回答说。
“这我已经看到了，”苍蝇“嗡嗡”地说，
“可你坐在这里干吗？”
“就是坐着呗！”小顽童说。
苍蝇想了想，说：“可是你总得干点儿什么
吧！”
“什么也不干！”小顽童说，“难道非得干
点什么吗？”
“瞧你问的，”苍蝇激动地说，“这可是世上
最重要的事情！比如我吧，我成天飞来飞去，见
什么都舔一口。你能到处飞，见东西就舔吗？”
“不能！”小顽童嘟囔了一句。
“原来是这样啊！”苍蝇嘲笑说，“居然有
人不知道活在世上干什么。你可真够傻的！简直
傻透了！”她绕着小顽童的头不停地飞着，嘴里
一个劲儿地说：“真傻……透了……一点儿用
处……也没有！”然后便飞走了。
page_text_en:
One day, Little Rascal sat in the corner of the sofa as usual.
At that moment, a fly buzzed around the room, and finally landed on his nose.
"Hello!" the fly greeted the teddy bear.
"Hello!" Little Rascal replied, giving a sidelong glance at the fly on his nose.
"How are you doing?" the fly asked.
"I'm sitting here," the teddy bear replied.
"I can see that," the fly buzzed, "but what are you doing here?"
"Just sitting!" Little Rascal said.
The fly thought for a moment and said, "But you must be doing something, right?"
"Doing nothing!" Little Rascal said, "Does it have to be something?"
"Look at you asking that," the fly said excitedly, "This is the most important thing in the world! For example, me—I fly around all day, licking everything I see. Can you fly around and lick things?"
"No!" Little Rascal mumbled.
"So that's how it is!" the fly laughed mockingly, "There are people who don't even know what to do in life. You're really foolish! Absolutely foolish!" She circled around Little Rascal's head, saying over and over, "So foolish... absolutely foolish... not a bit useful... nothing at all!" Then she flew away.
summary_zh: 小顽童坐在沙发角落，一只苍蝇飞来落在他鼻子上，两人展开对话。苍蝇认为活着必须有所作为，而小顽童认为什么都不干也没关系，苍蝇嘲笑他愚蠢后飞走了。

page_text_ocr_zh:
苍蝇的这番话引起了绒布熊的思考。
“是啊，” 他对自己说，“也许我真的太傻了。如果所有人都知道自己活在世上是为了什么，那我现在也想知道。我应该去打听打听，也许可以找到一个人，他能告诉我正确的答案。”
于是，他从沙发上滑下来，摇摇晃晃地动身了。
当他路过地下室的楼梯时，碰见了一只老鼠。
“你好！” 绒布熊客客气气地打了个招呼，
“我叫小顽童，我很想知道，我到这世上到底干什么来着。”
老鼠靠着后门，站起身来，从上到下打量着小顽童。
然后，不太好意思地说：“活着的唯一意义在于：狡猾一点，不让自己被逮住，多弄些奶酪和熏肉，养活全家。你能养家吗？”
“不能。” 小顽童说。
“可怜的家伙！” 老鼠叹了一口气，“那我也不知道，你活在世上究竟是为了什么？” 说完，便钻回自己的洞里去了。
小顽童无奈地耸耸肩，走出了房子。
page_text_en:
The fly's words sparked the teddy bear's thoughts.
"Yes," he said to himself, "maybe I'm really too foolish. If everyone knows why they're alive, then I want to know too. I should go and find out, perhaps I can find someone who can tell me the right answer."
So, he slid off the sofa and wobbled off.
As he passed the basement stairs, he met a mouse.
"Hello!" the teddy bear said politely, "My name is Little Rascal. I really want to know, why am I here in this world?"
The mouse leaned against the back door, stood up, and looked the little rascal up and down.
Then, somewhat awkwardly, he said, "The only meaning of life is to be cunning, avoid getting caught, gather more cheese and bacon, and support your family. Can you support a family?"
"No," Little Rascal replied.
"Poor fellow!" the mouse sighed, "Then I don't know either, what exactly you're here for in this world." And with that, he scurried back into his hole.
Little Rascal shrugged helplessly and left the house.
summary_zh: 绒布熊小顽童在苍蝇的启发下开始思考生命的意义，他向一只老鼠询问，但老鼠认为活着的意义是养家糊口，小顽童无法做到，最终老鼠也表示自己不知道答案，小顽童无奈地离开了房子。

page_text_ocr_zh:
门前有一个开满鲜花的小花园。绒布熊坐在草丛中，看见一只蜜蜂不停地在花丛间飞。
“喂，请听我说……”小顽童喊道，“我有一个问题想问问你……”
“我忙着呢，没有时间！”蜜蜂“嗡嗡”地叫着，很快又飞到另一朵花上。
“也许你知道，活着到底是为了什么？”小顽童问。
“当然啦！”蜜蜂说，“打小就知道，活着的目的就是努力工作——不停地干活，永不偷懒，难道这点你都不明白吗？”
“努力？”小顽童问，“怎么才算努力呢？”
“辛勤采蜜，筑造蜂房，造福国家——难道你做不到吗？”
“不能！”小顽童回答说。
一听这话，蜜蜂火了：“我可没时间跟你这种废物瞎扯！赶紧走开，让我干活！要不我会蛰你的！”
绒布熊可不想冒这个险，连忙跑开了。
page_text_en:
There was a small garden full of flowers in front of the house. The teddy bear sat in the grass, watching a bee flying busily among the flowers.
"Hey, listen to me..." Little Rascal called out, "I have a question I want to ask you..."
"I'm busy, no time!" the bee buzzed, quickly flying to another flower.
"Maybe you know, what is life for?" Little Rascal asked.
"Of course!" the bee said, "Since I was little, I've known that the purpose of life is to work hard—never stop working, never be lazy. Don't you understand that?"
"Hard work?" Little Rascal asked, "What counts as hard work?"
"Diligently collecting honey, building beehives, benefiting the country—can't you do that?"
"No, I can't!" Little Rascal replied.
Hearing that, the bee got angry: "I don't have time to waste with you, you useless thing! Get away, let me work! Or I'll sting you!"
The teddy bear didn't want to take that risk, so he hurried away.
summary_zh: 绒布熊小顽童在花园里遇到一只忙碌的蜜蜂，他向蜜蜂询问活着的意义，蜜蜂认为活着就是努力工作，但小顽童无法做到，蜜蜂因此生气并驱赶他，小顽童只好跑开。

page_text_ocr_zh:
当他来到街上的时候，遇到了一只很脏的小鸟，他正在一个脏水坑里洗澡呢。
“哎，我说，”小鸟叫道，“你在那里面傻看什么？你没见过洗澡哇？
“见过，”小顽童回答说，“我也常常洗澡。但是，我可从来没有像你那样溅得到处都是水。”
“这关你什么事？”小鸟说，“你到底想干什么？
“我想知道，我到底活在世上干什么。”
“你该干什么，这关我屁事。不过，哥儿们，我给你个好主意。跟我学吧，别去管这些愚蠢的问题。你应该对什么都不满意，对什么都不在乎，那你就什么都不怕了。只有这点才是重要的。”
小顽童想了想，然后摇了摇头，叹了口气说：“可我一定要知道，一个旧绒布熊到底有些什么用处。”
小鸟大声嘲笑了一番，飞走了。
page_text_en:
When he arrived on the street, he met a very dirty little bird who was bathing in a muddy puddle.
"Hey, I'm telling you," the bird called out, "what are you staring at in there? Haven't you ever seen a bath?"
"I have," Little Rascal replied, "I bathe often too. But I've never splashed water everywhere like you do."
"What's it to you?" the bird said. "What do you want to do anyway?"
"I want to know, what am I supposed to do in this world."
"What you should do? That's none of my business. But hey, here's a good idea. Follow me. Don't bother with these silly questions. You should be dissatisfied with everything, care about nothing, and then you won't be afraid of anything. That's the only thing that matters."
Little Rascal thought for a moment, shook his head, and sighed, "But I must know, what use is an old rag doll bear?"
The bird laughed loudly and flew away.
summary_zh: 小顽童在街上遇到一只在脏水坑里洗澡的小鸟，他向小鸟询问活着的意义，小鸟建议他不要在乎任何事，但小顽童仍坚持想找到自己的价值，最终小鸟嘲笑他后飞走了。

page_text_ocr_zh:
小顽童又陷入了深深的思考，脚步沉重地沿街向前走去。他来到了一个公园。公园中间有一个蓝色的湖。波光粼粼的湖面上，一只美丽的白天鹅正在快乐地游着。
“你可真美！”小顽童赞美道。
“我知道。”天鹅说着展开翅膀，像一面鼓起的风帆。
“那你活着的目的是什么？”小顽童很想知道。
“多么愚蠢的问题！”天鹅严肃地回答说，“生活最根本的意义在于美。仅仅在于美。否则还有什么？”他美滋滋地打量着水中自己的影子。“我生活的目的，就是履行这一最崇高的使命。你呢？”
小顽童也看了看自己水中的模样，然后很真诚地说：“不知道。”
“那么说，你可真是多余的。”天鹅说着，脸上露出高傲的微笑。他又向湖中游去，看都不愿再看一眼这只破旧的绒布熊。
page_text_en:
Little Rascal was lost in deep thought, walking slowly down the street. He arrived at a park. In the middle of the park was a blue lake. On the shimmering water, a beautiful white swan was swimming happily.
"You're so beautiful!" Little Rascal praised.
"I know," the swan said, spreading its wings like a billowing sail.
"Then what is the purpose of your life?" Little Rascal wanted to know.
"What a foolish question!" the swan replied seriously. "The most fundamental meaning of life is beauty. Beauty alone. What else could there be?" He proudly admired his reflection in the water. "The purpose of my life is to fulfill this most noble mission. And you?"
Little Rascal looked at his own reflection in the water, then honestly said, "I don't know."
"Then you are truly superfluous," the swan said, a proud smile on his face. He swam back into the lake, not even bothering to look back at the old rag doll.
summary_zh: 小顽童来到公园的湖边，向一只白天鹅询问活着的意义。天鹅认为生命的意义在于美，并因小顽童无法理解而认为他多余，最终不屑地游走。

page_text_ocr_zh:
湖的对面是一片森林，小顽童朝那边走去。不一会儿，他遇见了一只布谷鸟，鸟儿坐在树枝上，不断地发出同一种声音。
“你在干什么呢？”小顽童问。
“我在数数，别打断我！”布谷鸟回答说，
“65、66、67……”
“你在数什么？”
“我什么都数：树、树叶、冷杉球果，数天数，数钟点……什么都数。别打断我，68、69、70……”
“这有什么意义吗？”小顽童问。
“那还用问！”布谷鸟回答说，“什么都取决于数。能够数的东西，才是真实的。不能数的东西，都不能算数。”
“那么，”小顽童满怀希望地问，“也许你能把我也算上？”
“好的，”布谷鸟说，“那你看看自己应该归到哪一类吧。”
“我没法归进某一类，”小顽童承认道，
“我只是我自己。”
“那就没法算上你了，”布谷鸟说，“别再打断我。”说完，布谷鸟飞走了。从远处还不断传来他的数数声。不知又在数什么呢。
page_text_en:
Across the lake was a forest, and Little Rascal walked toward it. Soon, he met a cuckoo bird sitting on a branch, constantly making the same sound.
"What are you doing?" Little Rascal asked.
"I'm counting, don't interrupt me!" the cuckoo replied,
"65, 66, 67..."
"What are you counting?"
"I count everything: trees, leaves, pine cones, days, hours... everything. Don't interrupt me, 68, 69, 70..."
"Does that have any meaning?" Little Rascal asked.
"Why even ask!" the cuckoo replied, "Everything depends on counting. Only things that can be counted are real. Things that can't be counted don't count at all."
"Then," Little Rascal asked hopefully, "maybe you could count me too?"
"Alright," the cuckoo said, "then see which category you belong to."
"I can't fit into any category," Little Rascal admitted,
"I'm just myself."
"Then you can't be counted," the cuckoo said, "Don't interrupt me anymore." And with that, the cuckoo flew away. From afar, his counting voice continued to echo. Who knows what he was counting now.
summary_zh: 小顽童在森林里遇到一只布谷鸟，布谷鸟正在专注地数数，认为只有能被数清的东西才是真实的。小顽童请求被算入其中，但因自己无法归类而被拒绝，布谷鸟最终飞走，继续数数。

page_text_ocr_zh:
旧绒布熊朝森林深处走去，树林越来越密，越来越黑。树藤挂在树枝上，挡住了路。这是真正的热带丛林。
在他头顶上，一群猴子在高高的树枝间尖叫着爬来爬去。当猴子们看见绒布熊时，突然安静下来。猴头从树上跳下来，站在小顽童面前。
“你来这里找什么？”他龇牙咧嘴地问。
“我不想打扰你们，”小顽童很有礼貌地说，
“我只是想问问，我们这样活着的目的是什么？”
猴子们七嘴八舌地说开了：“他想知道，像我们这样的活着的目的是什么，他居然问，像我们这样的活着干吗……”
“住嘴！”猴头大吼一声，龇着牙齿。
当大家重新安静下来后，他说：“活着的惟一目的是去组织和建立一些团体，如协会、俱乐部、委员会、党派——任何一个团体都成。反正我们一直是这样做的。”
“为什么？”，小顽童问。
“这很重要，”猴头说，“一个人发号施令，其他人都服从。否则一切都会乱套。每个人都应该拥有自己的准确位置，这样他才知道自己的价值。你能领导别人吗？或者你听从别人的指挥？”
“都不行。”小顽童说。
“那你不能加入我们的行列！”猴头大叫。
其他猴子纷纷用能抓到手的所有东西朝小顽童扔过来。吓得他急忙跑开了。
page_text_en:
The old rag doll bear walked deeper into the forest. The trees became denser and darker. Vines hung from branches, blocking the path. This was a true tropical jungle.
Above him, a group of monkeys screeched and climbed among the high branches. When they saw the rag doll bear, they suddenly fell silent. The monkey leader jumped down from the tree and stood before the little rascal.
"What are you looking for here?" he asked, baring his teeth.
"I don't want to disturb you," the little rascal said politely,
"I just want to ask, what is the purpose of our lives?"
The monkeys started chattering: "He wants to know what the purpose of our lives is. He actually asks, what's the point of living like us..."
"Shut up!" the monkey leader roared, baring his teeth.
When everyone quieted down again, he said: "The only purpose of living is to organize and build groups, like associations, clubs, committees, political parties—any group will do. That's what we've always done."
"Why?" the little rascal asked.
"It's very important," the monkey leader said, "One person gives orders, and everyone else obeys. Otherwise, everything will fall into chaos. Everyone should have their exact place, so they know their value. Can you lead others? Or do you obey others' commands?"
"Neither," the little rascal said.
"Then you can't join our ranks!" the monkey leader shouted.
The other monkeys threw everything they could grab at the little rascal. Scared, he hurried away.
summary_zh: 绒布熊小顽童进入热带丛林，向一群猴子询问活着的意义。猴头认为生命的意义在于组织团体并确立个人位置，因小顽童既不能领导也不能服从，被拒绝加入并遭到驱赶，小顽童只得仓皇逃离。

page_text_ocr_zh:
在原始森林的后面，是一片广阔的草原。一群大象正在进行非常严肃认真的谈话。他们都长着张充满智慧的脸，一举一动都很庄重威严。
“对不起！”小顽童有些胆怯地问，“你们能告诉我，一个人活在世上究竟是为了什么吗？”
大象听了，连忙将他团团围住，皱着眉头低头打量着他。
“这是一个非常深刻的问题，我们已经想了很长时间。”一头大象说。
“那结果呢？”小顽童充满期待地问，“你们找到答案了吗？”
“对于深刻的问题必须进行全面彻底的思考，”另一头大象说，“我们不能草率从事。所以，活着的意义恰恰在于认真思考生活的意义。”
“但是，”小顽童忍不住插话道，“那可是没完没了的，我不知道自己能不能等得到。”
“就算这样吧，”第三头大象开口了，“可你毕竟有一颗永远不死的灵魂——像所有生物一样，不是吗？或者你能告诉我，你的身体内有些什么？”
“我还从来没有仔细查看过，”小顽童承认，“但是，我想，可能是些木屑和泡沫塑料之类。”
“那么说，你根本就不是真正的生物，”第一头大象严厉地说，“你只不过是一个人造的东西，没有灵魂，没有思想。如果你什么都不是，那就应该把你扔掉。”
page_text_en:
Behind the primeval forest lies a vast grassland. A group of elephants are engaged in a very serious and earnest conversation. They all have wise-looking faces, and every move they make is solemn and dignified.
"Sorry!" the little rascal asked timidly, "Can you tell me, what is the purpose of living in this world?"
The elephants, upon hearing this, quickly surrounded him, frowning and looking down at him.
"This is a very profound question. We have been thinking about it for a long time," said one elephant.
"And what is the result?" the little rascal asked eagerly, "Have you found an answer?"
"For profound questions, we must conduct thorough and comprehensive thinking," said another elephant, "We cannot act rashly. Therefore, the meaning of life lies precisely in seriously contemplating the meaning of life itself."
"But," the little rascal couldn't help interjecting, "That could go on forever. I don't know if I can wait that long."
"Even so," the third elephant spoke up, "You surely have an immortal soul—just like all living beings, right? Or can you tell me, what's inside your body?"
"I've never really looked inside carefully," the little rascal admitted, "But I think it might be wood shavings and foam plastic or something like that."
"Then you are not a true living being at all," the first elephant said sternly, "You are merely a man-made thing, without a soul, without thought. If you are nothing at all, then you should be thrown away."
summary_zh: 小顽童在草原上遇到一群正在严肃讨论生命意义的大象，他向它们提问，大象们认为生命的意义在于思考，但当小顽童无法证明自己有灵魂时，被判定为非生物并遭到驱逐。

page_text_ocr_zh:
听到这，可怜的旧绒布熊第一次真正感到了难过——虽然他是用木屑和泡沫塑料做的。即使他没有特别的要求和权利，那他也不愿被人扔掉。他摇摇晃晃地走了，再也没有什么兴趣找任何人询问活着的目的了。草原上沙子和石头越来越多。小顽童已经很累了，他靠着一块岩石坐了下来，让太阳照在他那打了补丁的肚子上。
突然，只听身边传来尖声尖气的说话声：
“嘿，小胖子，真是太巧了！”他转过身来，看见一条巨大的响尾蛇，她正用发亮的眼睛盯着自己，玩具熊想赶紧跑开，但他已经不能动弹了。
“站着别动，小东西！”大蛇吐着舌头说，
“不然我会生气的。”响尾蛇慢慢地把头扬到绒布熊面前。“怎么样？宝贝，”她面对面地冲小顽童说，“来得正好，你很合我的口味。”
“谢……谢谢！”小顽童吓得结结巴巴的，
“但是，对不起，我该走了。”
“我必须搞清楚，自己活着是为了什么？”
大蛇阴阳怪气地笑了笑：“可这不是什么问题。像你这样的，活着的目的就是让我吃掉。我很想吃你，小胖子。你是可以吃的，不是吗？”
“我希望不是，”小顽童答道，“我身体里面只有木屑和泡沫塑料。”
“是吗？”大蛇很失望，“那你真是什么用处也没有。我只好去找别的东西吃了。”她招呼也没打，就很快爬走了。
page_text_en:
Hearing this, the poor old rag doll bear felt truly sad for the first time—though he was made of wood shavings and foam plastic. Even without special demands or rights, he didn’t want to be thrown away. He shuffled away, no longer interested in asking anyone about the purpose of life. The grassland had more and more sand and stones. The little rascal was very tired; he leaned against a rock and sat down, letting the sun shine on his patched-up belly.

Suddenly, a sharp, high-pitched voice came from nearby:
"Hey, little fatty, what a coincidence!" He turned around and saw a huge rattlesnake, her bright eyes fixed on him. The toy bear tried to run away, but he couldn’t move.

"Stay still, little thing!" the big snake hissed,
"Or I’ll get angry." The rattlesnake slowly raised her head toward the rag doll bear. "How’s it going, sweetie?" she said directly to the little rascal, "Perfect timing—you’re just my taste!"

"Th-thank you..." the little rascal stammered, frightened,
"But, sorry, I should go now."

"I must figure out why I’m alive!"

The snake sneered: "That’s not a problem. For someone like you, the purpose of life is to be eaten by me. I really want to eat you, little fatty. You’re edible, aren’t you?"

"I hope not," the little rascal replied, "My body is only filled with wood shavings and foam plastic."

"Really?" the snake said, disappointed. "Then you’re truly useless. I’ll just go find something else to eat." She didn’t even say goodbye and quickly slithered away.
summary_zh: 小顽童在草原上感到疲惫和绝望，正坐着休息时，被一条响尾蛇发现。蛇认为小顽童是食物，但当得知他体内只有木屑和泡沫塑料后，觉得他毫无用处，便失望地离开。

page_text_ocr_zh:
小顽童松了一口气，连忙逃走了，他那小短腿能跑得多快就有多快。他匆匆逃离了荒漠，又来到了一片草地上。直到胸口跑疼了，才停了下来。他发现自己正站在一丛灌木前。灌木的小树枝上挂着一团闪闪发光的丝线。正当他在仔细打量时，小线团突然裂开了，一只蝴蝶从里面挣脱飞了出来，阳光下，他那五彩缤纷的翅膀张开了。
“真是太奇妙了！你是怎么做到这点的？”
小顽童充满钦佩和赞叹地问道。
“就这么做了呗！” 蝴蝶细声细气地说，
“最开始的时候我是一只卵，后来变成了小毛虫，再后来我变成了蛹，现在就变成蝴蝶啦。我们来到世上的目的就是不断提高和升华自己。你难道不能使自己得到提高和升华吗？”
“不能！” 绒布熊说。
“那你活在世上干吗？” 蝴蝶不解地问。还没等绒布熊回答，他已经开始翩翩起舞了。
“说的是，” 小顽童小声地嘟囔道，“这也是我一直很想知道的。”
page_text_en:
The little rascal sighed in relief and hurried away, his short legs running as fast as they could. He quickly fled the desert and arrived at a grassy field. Only when his chest ached from running did he stop. He found himself standing before a bush. On a small branch of the bush hung a shimmering cocoon. As he examined it closely, the cocoon suddenly split open, and a butterfly emerged, spreading its colorful wings in the sunlight.
"How wonderful! How did you do that?" the little rascal asked, full of admiration and awe.
"That's just how it's done!" the butterfly said softly,
"At first, I was an egg, then I became a caterpillar, then a chrysalis, and now I'm a butterfly. The purpose of our existence is to constantly improve and elevate ourselves. Can't you also improve and elevate yourself?"
"No!" the rag doll bear said.
"Then why are you alive?" the butterfly asked, puzzled. Before the rag doll bear could answer, the butterfly had already begun to dance gracefully.
"That's right," the little rascal murmured quietly, "that's exactly what I've always wanted to know."
summary_zh: 小顽童在逃离响尾蛇后，来到一片草地，发现一只蝴蝶从茧中破茧而出。他向蝴蝶询问生命的意义，蝴蝶认为生命的意义在于不断自我提升和升华。小顽童因无法做到而感到困惑，但最终从蝴蝶的蜕变中找到了自己一直想了解的答案。

page_text_ocr_zh:
就在这时，一位小姑娘走了过来，她光着脚，身上的衣服很破旧，因为她的父母太穷，没法给她买新衣服。
看见绒布熊后，她停了下来。睁大双眼看着他问：“你叫什么名字？”
“小顽童！”绒布熊说。
“你是一只绒布熊，对吗？”小姑娘问，“我还从来没有过一只绒布熊，你愿意归我吗？”
“很乐意！”小顽童说，他感到心里暖烘烘的——尽管他是用木屑和泡沫塑料做的。
小姑娘把他抱在怀里。并吻了他的鼻子。
从此，小顽童又有了自己的主人。他俩都感到很幸福。
但是，这个故事还没有结束。
几天以后，那只讨厌的苍蝇又来找小顽童。还没等她看见绒布熊，就又开始在他头顶“嗡嗡嗡”地叫了起来：“你来到世上有什么用？你真傻……傻傻……一点儿用处……也没有……”
但是，这次小顽童知道自己该怎么办了。
“啪”的一声！——苍蝇终于住嘴了。
page_text_en:
At that moment, a little girl came over. She was barefoot, and her clothes were worn and old, because her parents were too poor to buy her new ones.
When she saw the rag doll, she stopped. She opened her eyes wide and asked him, "What's your name?"
"Little Rascal!" the rag doll said.
"You're a rag doll, right?" the little girl asked. "I've never had a rag doll before. Would you like to belong to me?"
"Very gladly!" Little Rascal said, feeling warm inside—despite being made of wood shavings and foam plastic.
The little girl held him in her arms and kissed his nose.
From then on, Little Rascal had his own owner again. Both of them felt very happy.
But the story wasn't over yet.
A few days later, that annoying fly came back to find Little Rascal. Before she even saw the rag doll, she started buzzing above his head: "What use are you in this world? You're so silly... silly... absolutely useless... nothing at all..."
But this time, Little Rascal knew what to do.
"Smack!"—the fly finally stopped buzzing.
summary_zh: 小顽童被一位贫穷的小姑娘收养，重新拥有了主人，感到幸福。但讨厌的苍蝇再次出现，嘲笑他无用，小顽童这次果断拍死了它，找到了自己的价值。
